ambiguity.finding: The Non-Functional Requirements section uses vague, unmeasurable language ('fast and responsive', 'reasonable throughput under normal load', 'scale appropriately as needed', 'robust under several kinds of failure') instead of concrete, checkable criteria.

nfrs.finding: The Non-Functional Requirements section makes quantitative-type claims about speed, throughput, scalability and failure robustness without stating any number or unit.
